newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nail says Gold Fields talks continuing.
newsitem.headline: Nail says Gold Fields talks continuing.

text.p: South African black investment group New Africa Investments Ltd (Nail) said on Thursday that talks with mining house Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd and Driefontein Consolidated Ltd were continuing.
The firm advised its shareholders to exercise caution if dealing in the group's shares.
Last month Nail said it was in talks with Rembrandt Group Ltd to take control of Gold Fields, the world's third largest gold producer.

In a cautionary notice to shareholders on May 15, Nail said it was in dicussions with Gold Fields and its Driefontein Consolidated Ltd unit to acquire their shareholdings in Asteroid Ltd, which holds 40 percent of GFSA Holdings Ltd.
"The successful conclusion of these discussions would result in a partnership being formed between Rembrandt Group Ltd and Nail in GFSA Holdings Ltd," it said then.

The deal, if successful, would mark a further big advance for black business in South Africa -- and a significant coup for Nail which already has control of industrial group Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd.

Gold Fields would provide a major presence in the mining industry, something Nail is believed to be keen to achieve. Nail had been seen as a potential bidder for a stake in rival mining house JCI Ltd, but that deal was finally clinched by another black empowerment consortium, African Mining Group, led by Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd.
However, in a recent interview Nail deputy chairman Cyril Ramaphosa said the discussions could take some time before a concrete deal is sealed.
Gold Fields and Driefontein also issued cautionary notices on Thursday, saying the talks with Nail were ongoing and warning shareholders to be careful when dealing in their shares.
